true_wording: Two items faithful. The first drops 'NWS/OSHA', which changes who had not recommended. Say: 'That office wrote that there were no official weather service or OSHA recommendations for sheltering at work, no guidance on what types of warnings to shelter for, and no different shelters for businesses with large warehouse construction.' On-screen lines must be the AAR words verbatim, ellipsis marked, attributed 'WFO St. Louis after-action review, quoted in the Service Assessment, p33-34'.
source: NWS Joint Regional Service Assessment (1 Jun 2023)
verbatim_quote: (no official NWS/Occupational Safety & Health Administration (OSHA) recommendations for severe weather sheltering guidelines in the workplace, no guidance on what types of warnings to shelter for, no differentiation in shelters for businesses with large warehouse construction, etc.)..

claim: 'nobody had told big workplaces what to do' (angle claim)
true_wording: Angle accepted, not re-judged. Risk: OSHA says it 'recommends' severe weather emergency plans and its letter gave Amazon specific recommendations, so keep the claim tied to weather-service sheltering guidance.
source: https://www.osha.gov/news/newsreleases/chicago/20220426
verbatim_quote: OSHA does not have a standard that requires severe weather emergency plans but recommends them

source: NWS Joint Regional Service Assessment (1 Jun 2023)
verbatim_quote: An Amazon warehouse suffered extensive damage from this tornado at approximately 8:27 P.M. CST.

claim: the warning had been out about twenty-five minutes
true_wording: SA p29 does mean the tornado warning ('tornado warning and additional information'), 25 min. But SA p28 says the warning that included Madison County was issued 8:06 PM, which is 21 minutes. Safe wording true under both: 'and the tornado warning had been out for more than twenty minutes.' If keeping 25, attribute: 'the Weather Service says the warning came about twenty-five minutes before'. Same issue in T1-S1 chip 'about 25 min' and the A1 title (outside this slice).
source: NWS Joint Regional Service Assessment (1 Jun 2023)
verbatim_quote: The tornado warning and additional information was provided approximately 25 minutes prior to the warehouse being hit.

claim: Inside, the story of those minutes starts with a megaphone
true_wording: Fact is in OSHA's own letter (first listed risk factor), not only AP. Narration is unattributed and 'starts with' implies cause; attribute: 'Inside, OSHA's letter lists a megaphone first: the one meant to start the shelter plan was locked in a cage.' No blame wording. Claims Journal AP page not retrieved; primary letter used instead.
source: OSHA Hazard Alert Letter to Amazon, 26 Apr 2022
verbatim_quote: The megaphone, identified by the Emergency Action Plan (EAP) to be used to activate the shelter-in-place procedure, was locked in a cage and not accessible.

claim: Edwardsville met the minimum the federal rules asked for
true_wording: OSHA said 'guidelines', and also that no standard requires such plans, so 'rules' is false. Say: 'OSHA said Amazon's severe weather procedures met minimal federal safety guidelines for storm sheltering.'
source: OSHA Chicago release, 26 Apr 2022
verbatim_quote: Amazon's severe weather emergency procedures met minimal federal safety guidelines for storm sheltering

claim: What I couldn't find was anyone who'd told a building that big what the minimum should be
true_wording: Cut 'anyone': OSHA gave Amazon recommendations and recommends plans. Source-backed replacement: 'The Weather Service's own review says it had no guidance for a building that big.' (attributed to the AAR, SA p33-34).
source: NWS Joint Regional Service Assessment (1 Jun 2023)
verbatim_quote: no differentiation in shelters for businesses with large warehouse construction
